make-bee-frames-desc: Two panels, three sticks and a resin make two empty frames, in the crafting grid. Put each frame in the rack and use a liner on it: bees only build comb on lined frames.
assemble-langstroth-desc: Place the base. Open a super, fill it with lined frames, close it, pick it up and use it on the base. Put the populated brood box on top. Tick this off when the bees are at work. Take full frames to the rack and scrape them with a knife for honeycomb.
make-sewing-kit-tailorsdelight: Four flax twine, a stick and a needle make a sewing kit, in the crafting grid. The needle is used up. Some clothes need a sewing kit, and it mends worn clothing and armor.
make-sack-tailorsdelight: Linen, flax twine and a needle make a sack, in the crafting grid. Wear it in a bag slot to carry more.
knap-awl-desc: An awl bores holes in leather and heavy cloth, and needles, buttons and backpacks all need one. Knap one from flint, or put a bone, a stone and a knife in the crafting grid.
make-needle-desc: A bone, an awl and a knife make two bone needles, in the crafting grid. Antler gives horn needles, more of them from a bigger rack. Sewing kits and sacks now take a needle.
dye-thread-desc: Seal flax twine in a barrel with half a litre of woad dye for each, to make blue thread. Other colors take mordanted twine: soak it in diluted alum first, then in the dye.
checkered-cloth-desc: Put a sewing kit in the middle of the crafting grid, colored thread in the corners and flax twine on the sides to make checkered cloth.
make-backpack-tailorsdelight: Eight leather, leather strips, buttons, flax twine and an awl make a backpack, in the crafting grid. Wear it in a bag slot: it holds far more than a sack.
make-buttons-desc: A bone, a stick, an awl and a knife make a set of buttons and clasps, in the crafting grid. Antler makes horn buttons. Backpacks need them now.
leather-strips-desc: Cut a piece of leather into strips with a knife, in the crafting grid. Backpacks need them for straps.
dark-leather-desc: Seal a piece of leather in a barrel with two litres of strong tannin for a day to make dark brown leather.
smith-awl-desc: Stone and bone awls blunt quickly. Smith an awl thorn on the anvil and put it on a stick for one that lasts.
cast-buttons-desc: Form a button mold from clay and fire it. Pour copper into it, as into any tool mold, for copper buttons.
shear-animal-desc: Sheep, goats, deer, elk, moose and gazelle grow fleece once bred in captivity. Use shears or a knife on one: a knife is likelier to hurt it. The fleece grows back. See animal shearing.
make-shears-desc: Smith shears on the anvil. They shear more fleece than a knife, and hurt the animal less.
wash-fleece-desc: Raw fleece is dirty. Seal it in a barrel with half a litre of limewater each for most of a day, and it comes out as clean wool fibers. See wool and knitting.
spin-wool-desc: Four wool fibers make a length of wool twine, in the crafting grid. Its color follows the fleece.
weave-wool-desc: Four lengths of wool twine around a stick make wool cloth, in the crafting grid. Some clothes can be sewn from it in place of linen cloth.
make-kneedles-desc: Two sticks and a knife make wooden knitting needles, in the crafting grid. Bone and antler make sturdier ones.
dye-wool-desc: Seal plain wool cloth in a barrel with half a litre of woad dye. Other dyes need mordanted wool first, soaked in diluted alum.
knit-sweater-desc: Knitting needles and wool twine make a sweater, worn over a shirt. Each pattern calls for particular colors: the gray one takes plain and gray twine, from a bighorn sheep's fleece. A few need the clothier class.
make-longbow-tailorsdelight: A dry long bowstave, flax twine, two leather strips and fat, resin or beeswax make a longbow. It shoots farther and harder than a simple bow.
make-jerkin-tailorsdelight: Leather, three leather strips and four dark blue threads make a jerkin, with an awl in the crafting grid. Seal blue thread in woad dye again to darken it. A jerkin is light armor on its own and the base of brigandine and chain.
make-leather-armor-tailorsdelight: Leather and flax twine make sewn leather armor, with an awl in the crafting grid: a good balance of protection and freedom to move.
make-gambeson-tailorsdelight: Layers of linen, three brown threads and buttons make gambeson armor, with an awl in the crafting grid. Brown thread is flax twine sealed in strong tannin. It protects well without slowing you much.
make-saddle-tailorsdelight: Leather, two nails and strips, two brown or black threads, an awl and a knife make a saddle. Brown thread is flax twine sealed in strong tannin. See the guide to mountable animals.
make-bridle-tailorsdelight: Leather strips, nails and strips, two brown or black threads and an awl make a bridle. A snaffle bit steers like walking; with a curb bit, press forward once to go and again to stop.
make-saddlebags-tailorsdelight: Leather, nails and strips, two brown or black threads and an awl make saddlebags. They go over the elk's haunches and carry extra goods.
make-pillion-tailorsdelight: Leather, leather strips, two brown or black threads and an awl make a pillion cushion. It goes behind the saddle and lets a second person ride, though only the front rider steers.
make-sails-tailorsdelight: Sails are linen stretched on support beams and sticks, sewn with flax twine and a needle, which is used up. Saw a debarked log into a support beam, then craft the sails; a recipe makes four.
